\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کولاک} (kulâk)}{کولاک (kulâk)}]{\fa{کولاک} (kulâk) — a snowstorm}

\label{lesson:FA-C476-kulak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a gale, then the Persian for a whirlwind.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کولاک}}
\textbf{\fa{کولاک}} (\emph{kulâk}) — \textquotedblleft{}a snowstorm\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کولاک} \fa{جاده} \fa{کوهستانی} \fa{را} \fa{بست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kulâk jâdde-ye kuhestâni râ bast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The snowstorm closed the mountain road.
\end{quote}

Snow with strong wind.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{kulâk} is not settled, and EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kulâk}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kulâk}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a gale, then the Persian for a whirlwind, then say \emph{kulâk} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بوران} (burân)}{بوران (burân)}]{\fa{بوران} (burân) — a blizzard (with driving snow)}

\label{lesson:FA-C476-buran}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a whirlwind, then the Persian for a snowstorm.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بوران}}
\textbf{\fa{بوران}} (\emph{burân}) — \textquotedblleft{}a blizzard (with driving snow)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{بوران} \fa{راننده} \fa{ها} \fa{جاده} \fa{را} \fa{نمیدیدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar burân rânande-hâ jâdde râ nemididand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the blizzard the drivers couldn't make out the road.
\end{quote}

Close in sense to \emph{kulâk}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{burân} is usually traced to Turkic \emph{buran} 'a snowstorm'. EtymDB lists an Arabic \emph{būrān} without a gloss, so the line is hedged.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{یخبندان} (yakhbandân)}{یخبندان (yakhbandân)}]{\fa{یخبندان} (yakhbandân) — a frost, freezing weather}

\label{lesson:FA-C476-yakhbandan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a snowstorm, then the Persian for a blizzard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{یخبندان}}
\textbf{\fa{یخبندان}} (\emph{yakhbandân}) — \textquotedblleft{}a frost, freezing weather\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{یخبندان} \fa{لوله} \fa{های} \fa{آب} \fa{ترکید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar yakhbandân lule-hâ-ye âb tarkid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the frost the water pipes burst.
\end{quote}

\emph{yakh} 'ice' + \emph{band} 'binding' + \emph{-ân}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{yakhbandân} is a native compound of \emph{yakh} 'ice', which EtymDB traces to Proto-Iranian \emph{aixa-}, \emph{band} 'binding', from the root of \emph{bastan}, and the ending \emph{-ân}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{یخ} \fa{زدن} (yakh zadan)}{یخ زدن (yakh zadan)}]{\fa{یخ} \fa{زدن} (yakh zadan) — to freeze}

\label{lesson:FA-C476-yakh-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a blizzard, then the Persian for a frost.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{یخ} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{یخ} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{yakh zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to freeze\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آب} \fa{حوض} \fa{شب} \fa{یخ} \fa{زد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Âb-e howz shab yakh zad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The water in the pool froze overnight.
\end{quote}

\emph{yakh} 'ice' + \emph{zadan}. Of people: \emph{yakh zadam} — I'm frozen.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{yakh zadan} is built from native \emph{yakh} 'ice', which EtymDB traces to Proto-Iranian \emph{aixa-}, and the native verb \emph{zadan} 'to strike'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آب} \fa{شدن} (âb shodan)}{آب شدن (âb shodan)}]{\fa{آب} \fa{شدن} (âb shodan) — to melt}

\label{lesson:FA-C476-ab-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a frost, then the Persian for to freeze.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آب} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{آب} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{âb shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to melt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{آفتاب} \fa{برفها} \fa{آب} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar âftâb barf-hâ âb shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The snow melted in the sun.
\end{quote}

Literally 'to become water'. Also to lose weight.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âb shodan} is built from \emph{âb} 'water', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{āb} (EtymDB), and the native verb \emph{shodan} 'to become'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
